subject: Request: Streaming endpoint pacing waiver & token-rate aperture for HelioHealth POC
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Yang <emma.yang@heliohealth.com>, Marc Liu <marc.liu@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Helio POC — streaming token pacing and SLA ask

Hi Emma / Marc —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As we scope the HelioHealth POC traffic profile we want to be explicit about a small SLA carveout we're requesting for streaming routes to match your integration patterns. In short:

- Goal: keep end-user interactivity (first token delivered) within a target window for short prompts, while allowing a slightly relaxed sustained token/s throughput when customers pump long generated documents in back-to-back requests during indexing jobs.
- Request: a temporary exception for the PoC where time-to-first-token (TTFT) target remains 300–450ms median, but we allow a sustained token/sec threshold of 35–45 tok/s (instead of our standard 60 tok/s) for non-priority background bursts.

Attached is a quick matrix comparing normal SLA vs requested PoC aperture, plus a sample traffic file. Can you confirm whether this tradeoff is acceptable for your end-to-end UX? If yes, we'll draft a short amendment to the trial agreement and include telemetry hooks for visibility.

Next steps:
- Emma/Marc: confirm acceptance or propose numeric changes by Fri 3/26
- Redwood: if accepted, we prepare amendment + run a one-hour sustained-burst run to validate degradation patterns

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Yang <emma.yang@heliohealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marc Liu <marc.liu@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helio POC — streaming token pacing and SLA ask

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment. High level we can accept an elevated sustained token/sec cap for background indexing as long as first-token latency for interactive sessions stays within the window you listed. A couple of clarifying questions:

1) How do you differentiate interactive vs background traffic (IP, route, API key tag, header)?
2) During the one-hour sustained-burst run, will Redwood apply any manual throttling or automatic fallback to a smaller model? We want to understand failure modes.

If you send a short amendment that includes observability (per-request token/time breakdown) and a rollback trigger (e.g., >5% of interactive requests exceed 600ms TTFT), I think Legal will be comfortable.

—Emma
VP Product, HelioHealth
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Yang <emma.yang@heliohealth.com>, Marc Liu <marc.liu@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helio POC — streaming token pacing and SLA ask

Emma — thanks, great questions. Quick answers: 

1) Traffic classification: we recommend tagging interactive sessions with an "x-redwood-mode: interactive" header (or separate API key). Background indexing jobs can use a different API key and route ("/v1/generate/background"). We'll include conditional routing rules in the amendment.

2) Failure modes: during the validation burst the platform will first try to autoscale (if Dedicated capacity is assigned). For the hosted PoC we will apply graceful degradation: fallback to the smaller-compatible model variant + queueing at a conservative token/sec threshold. We'll also emit a telemetry flag for any request that had a model fallback.

Action: looping in Tessa and Lauren to get the legal + sales amendment drafted. Sergio will outline operational controls (circuit breaker thresholds, rollout plan).

Attachment: redwood-pacing-proposal.pdf (proposal matrix and suggested amendment language)

Aditya
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Yang <emma.yang@heliohealth.com>, Marc Liu <marc.liu@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helio POC — streaming token pacing and SLA ask

Emma / Marc —

Thanks — happy to proceed with the proposed PoC aperture. To summarize the components we'll include in the amendment:

- Numeric carveout: TTFT median target: 300–450ms; interactive rollback trigger: >5% of interactive TTFT >600ms in any 1h window
- Sustained token/sec aperture for background route during PoC: 35–45 tok/s (hosted)
- Traffic separation: required header or API key for background vs interactive
- Fallback behavior: automatic downgrade to a compatible smaller model + explicit telemetry flag per request
- Observability: per-route token latency breakdown, monthly PoC dashboard access for HelioHealth (1-week retention)
- Term: PoC exception valid for 60 days from amendment signature; we will re-evaluate before any committed Dedicated purchase

Please confirm and we will route to Legal + Billing for the short amendment. If acceptable, I’ll ask Lauren to prepare the doc and Sergio to schedule the one-hour validation window (target next Wed 3/31).

Tessa Morgan
Head of Platform Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marc Liu <marc.liu@heliohealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Emma Yang <emma.yang@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helio POC — streaming token pacing and SLA ask

All —

We reviewed the summary with Legal. HelioHealth approves the PoC exception with the rollback trigger and observability requirements as written. A couple of logistics items:

- Please send the amendment and the one-hour validation run checklist so we can sign and schedule.
- For the validation run, we’ll provide two weeks notice and a representative sample of our traffic (see attached sample).

Looking forward —
Marc Liu
Director of Engineering, HelioHealth
